content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to turn technical details into clear documentation. This skill structures READMEs, API references, tutorials, and guides for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Creates README structures with features, installation, quick start, usage, configuration, troubleshooting, and license sections.
Drafts API documentation with purpose, parameters, return values, examples, and error guidance.
Builds tutorials with prerequisites, ordered steps, expected results, and next steps.
Applies style rules for active voice, short sentences, defined terms, and scannable headings.
Supports changelogs, release notes, onboarding guides, and architecture documentation.
limitations: It does not validate technical accuracy unless source material is provided.
It does not execute code samples or test installation commands.
It needs product context, audience level, and source references for complete documentation.
Security-sensitive commands in generated examples still require human review.

use_cases.title: Write Project READMEs
use_cases.description: Turn project notes into clear README pages with setup, quick start, usage, and troubleshooting sections.

use_cases.title: Document APIs
use_cases.description: Create endpoint or function references that explain inputs, outputs, examples, errors, and edge cases.

use_cases.title: Build User Guides
use_cases.description: Create tutorials, onboarding guides, and support content for users learning technical workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a README
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new project page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for [project name]. Include the audience, project goal, key features, installation steps, quick start, common usage, troubleshooting, and license notes.

prompt_templates.title: Document an API
prompt_templates.prompt: Document this API using clear sections for purpose, parameters, return values, examples, errors, and edge cases. Use the source details I provide: [paste details].

prompt_templates.title: Write a Tutorial
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for guided learning content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a beginner tutorial for [task]. Start with prerequisites, then provide numbered steps, expected results, common errors, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure Existing Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for improving a larger documentation set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review and restructure the following documentation for clarity, completeness, and scanning. Preserve technical meaning, remove duplication, identify gaps, and propose missing sections: [paste docs].

output_examples.input: A CLI tool that sorts files by size and exports CSV results.
output_examples.output: A README plan with a product summary, feature list, installation steps, quick start, usage examples, configuration notes, troubleshooting, and license section.

output_examples.input: A REST endpoint that creates projects and returns validation errors.
output_examples.output: An API reference page with purpose, parameters, return values, example scenarios, error table, and guidance for common failures.

output_examples.input: A complex setup process for new developers joining a service team.
output_examples.output: A tutorial outline with prerequisites, ordered setup steps, verification checks, common issues, and next steps for deeper learning.

best_practices: Provide the audience, product goal, and source details before requesting documentation.
Ask for examples, expected results, and common errors when creating guides.
Review generated commands, URLs, and configuration paths before publishing.
anti_patterns: Requesting complete documentation with no product context or source material.
Publishing generated command examples without verifying them in the target environment.
Mixing beginner setup steps and advanced reference details in one unstructured page.

faq.question: Can this skill create API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure endpoint and function references with parameters, returns, examples, errors, and edge cases.

faq.question: Does it test code samples?
faq.answer: No. It writes documentation and examples, but it does not run commands or verify code behavior.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it improve existing documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current text and ask for clearer structure, missing sections, or a specific style.

faq.question: Can it write for non-developers?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the audience level and ask for simpler wording, fewer assumptions, and more context.

faq.question: What should I include in a prompt?
faq.answer: Include the audience, goal, source details, required sections, examples, and any style or terminology rules.
